title: Year 3 reading check: The River Nile, with tracker
subject: English
source: Written for english/y3 lesson 87 (Year 3 reading assessment tracker (Summer 1, end of term))
intro: Lesson 87. Read the passage, then answer the questions. Teachers record the results in the tracker.

passage.title: The River Nile
paras: The Nile flows north through eleven African countries before it reaches the Mediterranean Sea. For thousands of years, farmers in Egypt depended on its yearly flood, which left rich, dark soil on the fields.

The flood came every summer, when heavy rain fell far away in the mountains of Ethiopia. Farmers waited for the water to go down, then sowed wheat and barley in the wet soil. Without the river, most of Egypt would be desert.

Today a great dam at Aswan controls the water, so the river no longer floods the fields each year. People still use the Nile for drinking water, farming and travel. Boats called feluccas sail along it, just as they have for thousands of years.

questions.q: Which way does the Nile flow?
How many countries does it flow through?
What did the yearly flood leave on the fields?
Why did farmers depend on the flood?
questions.a: It left rich soil, so their crops could grow.

questions.q: Where did the rain that caused the flood fall?
What does the dam at Aswan do?
questions.a: It controls the water, so the river no longer floods the fields.

questions.q: Give two ways people use the Nile today.
questions.a: Any two: drinking water, farming, travel.
A kind of boat that sails on the Nile.

questions.q: Summarise the passage in one sentence.
questions.a: The Nile is a long river that has helped people farm and travel for thousands of years.
